newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks up in late trade on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks up in late trade on electronics.

text.p: A strong technical rebound in the bellwether electronics sector pushed Taiwan's stock index sharply higher in late Thursday trade as investors hunted for bargains in the wake of a big recent selloff, brokers said.

The main index, boosted by the heavily weighted electronics, was up 192.2 points or 2.05 percent at 9,573.26 with 30 minutes to go at 0330 GMT, clawing its way back from a tumble of more than 450 points in two previous sessions.
Turnover was relatively heavy at T$124 billion.
The highly volatile electronics sector, the driving force behind the booming market for months, was red hot after a weeklong correction -- rising nearly six percent.
"Considering that the sector had fallen for five consecutive sessions, it is time for a rebound given the strong fundementals of the industry," said Ben Lee of Nomura Securities.
Electronics, which rose more than 100 percent in the first half of 1997, were driven lower in recent days by heavy profit-taking from local and foreign institutional investors.
Microchip maker United Microelectronics Corp was up the daily seven percent limit, or T$7.5, to T$120, while rival Taiwan Semiconductor was up T$8 to T$142. Chipmaker Winbond was up T$3.5 to T$65.5.
Computer leader Acer Inc had risen T$5 to T$95.
